To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) current value disclosures are more informative than historical cost disclosures, (2) current value disclosures lead to better decisions than historical cost disclosures and (3) the current cost disclosures used in our experiments were not more informative than the historical cost disclosures.
current cost disclosures are no better than historical cost disclosures for investment decisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of current value disclosures on the investment decisions made by financial statement users.
the impact of alternative accounting measurement methods on decision making.
the question of whether current cost information improves decision making in a competitive environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence that current cost information is useful for making investment decisions.
current cost information is not superior to historical cost information.
current value information does not appear to be useful for decision making in the context of our study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current value disclosures are not relevant for decision making.
current cost disclosures, in and of themselves, are not useful for decision making, although the usefulness of current cost information may be increased when it is combined with other information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
current value information may not be useful for making investment decisions.
current cost financial statements are no better than historical cost financial statements in terms of their ability to improve investment decisions.
, in the absence of current value financial reports, managers will not be motivated to use current values in making decisions.
